content.text:
Perfect! I found the information. Based on the Slack messages, I can now answer the question:

**Charlie** identified the recursive search infinite loop problem. 

In message M0026 in the #algorithms channel (2025-01-31 11:00:00), Charlie stated:

> "The recursive pruning was a red flag too. When pruning classifiers triggered their own search trees, we created infinite loops within loops. **Mathematical impossibility of convergence when search calls search calls search...**"

The **mathematical constraint** that Charlie discovered was that **convergence is mathematically impossible when search recursively calls search** (i.e., when pruning classifiers that are supposed to optimize the search themselves trigger additional search trees, creating infinite recursive loops with no convergence guarantee).

This was part of the cascade of failures where the pruning models' neural network inference could recursively call the same search optimization system they were trying to prune, creating an unbounded recursive cycle.
